mechanism_claims.claim_text: AD7 and AD8 have direct membrane-integrity evidence from TO/PI flow-cytometry testing against S. enterica and MRSA; the paper reports injured/dead/intact-cell distributions after 50 µM peptide treatment.
direct_assay_types: thiazole orange / propidium iodide microbial membrane-integrity flow cytometry

target_context.strain_context: methods list ATCC 14028 and ATCC BAA-41

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=8:Effects of cryptides on membrane permeabilisation and cell viability; xml:fig=3b

mechanism_claims.limitations: Direct membrane-integrity assay was only performed for AD7 and AD8; no direct intracellular-target or apoptosis mechanism is assigned to the other cryptides.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: AD4, AD7, AD8, AD11, and AD12 show antibiofilm activity against mature S. enterica and MRSA biofilms, but this is treated as an activity phenotype rather than a molecular mechanism.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Biofilm eradication and MBEC/MBEC50 values do not identify a molecular target; they are not promoted to direct mechanism evidence.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The paper frames cationic cryptide activity as membrane interaction/permeability based on peptide charge and AMP background, while keeping anticancer killing mechanism unassigned because no direct apoptosis/mitochondrial/nuclear assay is reported for these peptides.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Mechanistic background and discussion statements are hypothesis/context; direct mechanism is limited to the AD7/AD8 membrane-integrity assay.

adjudication_note: Automated mechanism placeholders were replaced with source-reviewed claims. Only AD7/AD8 membrane-integrity data are direct mechanism; biofilm and anticancer activity remain phenotype/context.
